extracted.intended_audience: Individuals and organizations applying for, receiving, or administering NIH grants (PD/PIs, institutional grants offices, grant administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Use the NIH Grants Policy Statement to prepare, submit, manage, and close out NIH grant applications and awards, ensuring compliance with NIH terms, conditions, public policy requirements, reporting, financial and administrative rules, and peer review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for registration in eRA Commons for organizations, PD/PIs, and other individuals participating in NIH application and RPPR processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: eRA Commons Registration for the Organization; for the PD/PI; for other individuals (see 2.2.1.1–2.2.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of NIH support mechanisms available for applicants and the characteristics of each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Application Information and Processes; used to determine appropriate funding mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility rules that determine which individuals and organizations may apply for specific NIH funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears across multiple sections (general eligibility, special eligibilities for training/fellowships, SBIR/STTR, foreign organizations, federal institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Award Instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The different legal/financial instruments NIH uses to provide support (grants, cooperative agreements, etc.) and how the term 'grant' is used in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions note that 'grant' is used to mean both grants and cooperative agreements unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct application formats and submission pathways (e.g., new, resubmission, renewal, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes modular vs non-modular, activity-code considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different kinds of NIH funding opportunity announcements and other funding-related notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes standard NOFOs and other funding-related notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Implications of Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal responsibilities and consequences associated with submitting NIH grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers representations, certifications, and possible legal ramifications of application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies Affecting Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies that affect how applications are prepared, submitted, and considered (resubmissions, investigator status, post-submission materials, UEI/SAM requirements, graduate student compensation, data sharing policies, AI use, biosketches, submission limits, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detailed subtopics: Direct Cost Limitations for Consortium Indirect Costs; Resubmission policies; New/ESI investigators; PD/PI assurance requirements; Post-Submission Materials; SAM/UEI; Graduate Student Compensation; DMS and GDS; Human fetal tissue; Biosketch requirements; Limits on submissions; Appropriate use of AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Required forms and application components needed for NIH submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 2.3.8 for specifics (form names, required sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Receipt Information and Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing receipt dates, deadlines, electronic submission requirements, late applications, continuous submission exceptions, similar/identical applications, non-conformity, and emergency exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections include electronic submission requirements, late applications, continuous submission for certain NIH federal advisory committee members, similar/identical applications, application non-conformity, natural disasters and other emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and Confidentiality of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on public availability of application and award information and protections for confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes availability of information and confidentiality provisions; guidance for handling sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting Sensitive Data and Information Used in Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and requirements for safeguarding sensitive data used in NIH-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers data protection standards and practices to be followed by recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Process — Initial Review Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities of reviewers and NIH staff during initial peer review of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers reviewer roles, conflict of interest handling, and review administration (see 2.4.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review — Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall impact concept used by reviewers to summarize the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a distinct review element (see 2.4.1.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Scored Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of scored criteria reviewers use to evaluate non-SRF-applicable activity codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.4.1.3 identifies the standard scored review criteria (detailed criteria appear elsewhere in the NIHGPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Additional Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional review criteria that may be scored beyond the standard scored criteria for certain activity codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.4.1.4 lists these additional criteria for non-SRF-applicable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Additional Review Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Other considerations reviewers must account for during review that may affect funding decisions (e.g., human subjects, vertebrate animals, inclusion, biohazards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2.4.1.5 for the list of additional review considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Review Framework (SRF)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternative review framework used for certain activity codes that simplifies standard review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.4.1.6 describes when SRF applies and how it modifies review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of Initial Scientific Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and grounds for appealing initial scientific review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.4.2 covers appeal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Advisory Council or Board Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The role and process of advisory council/board review after initial peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.4.3 outlines the council/board review stage and considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Award Processes — Just-in-Time Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Just-in-Time (JIT) requests and documentation NIH may request prior to award (e.g., other support, IRB approvals, IACUC approvals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2.5.1; JIT timing and required materials are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Award — Submitting Revised Project Summaries/Specific Aims/Public Health Relevance Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for submitting revised abstracts/aims/relevance statements during pre-award adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.5.2 describes allowable revised materials and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining Applicant Organization and Individual Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures used by NIH to confirm institutional and individual eligibility for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 2.5.3 and 2.5.4 detail eligibility determination steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Analysis and Assessment of Management Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH review of applicant financial and management systems and cost proposals during pre-award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2.5.5 covers cost analysis and institutional system assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of Terms and Conditions — Federalwide Standard Terms and Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The general federal terms and conditions that govern grants and the NIH-specific terms that apply to NIH awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part II overview (chapter 3) for relationship to standard federal grant terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Policy Requirements and Objectives — Animal Welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for animal welfare assurances, IACUC approvals, foreign recipients, reporting to OLAW, and consortium responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Animal Welfare Assurance Requirements, Verification of IACUC Approval, Consortia rules, Foreign performance site specifics, and reporting to OLAW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Policy Requirements — Civil Rights Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Nondiscrimination requirements under Civil Rights Act, Education Amendments, Rehabilitation Act, Age Discrimination Act, LEP, and nondiscrimination in health programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections 4.1.2.1–4.1.2.6 enumerate statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials Registration and Reporting in ClinicalTrials.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing registration and results reporting for NIH-funded clinical trials, including NIH dissemination policy, FDAAA, and Good Cause Extension requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers NIH Policy on Dissemination of NIH-Funded Clinical Trial Information; FDAAA provisions; GCE requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality (Certificates of Confidentiality and Patient Record Protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for protecting confidential research data including Certificates of Confidentiality and confidentiality for alcohol/substance-use and HIPAA-protected records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 4.1.4 and related subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for disclosure, management, and reporting of investigator financial conflicts of interest in NIH-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Located under public policy requirements; see reporting and management obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive requirements for human subjects research: Federalwide Assurance, IRB approval certification, reporting to OHRP, data and safety monitoring, inclusion across lifespan, inclusion of women and minorities, GCP training, single IRB policy, and education requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections 4.1.16.1–4.1.16.10 list specific institutional and investigator obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Research Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions, prohibitions, and policies regarding NIH funding of human pluripotent stem cell research, including prohibited activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4.1.14.1 specifies prohibitions and applicability of NIH funding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Fetal Tissue Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and subcategories governing transplantation and non-transplantation research involving human fetal tissue from elective abortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 4.1.15.1–4.1.15.2 outline requirements and allowable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigational New Drug Applications/Investigational Device Exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and requirements when NIH-funded research involves IND/IDE-regulated activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4.1.17 addresses coordination with FDA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on use of NIH grant funds for lobbying and related disclosure/penalty rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 4.1.18 for details on prohibitions and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Statutory/Administrative Requirements (e.g., Fly America Act, FFATA, FISMA, Debarment, Drug-Free Workplace)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various federal requirements and mandates that NIH recipients must comply with, including travel (Fly America), vendor reporting (FFATA), information security (FISMA), debarment/suspension rules, and drug-free workplace obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple subsections (4.1.8–4.1.12, 4.1.5–4.1.7, 4.1.2, etc.) list specific statutes and resulting recipient duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation Mandates (Acknowledgment and Restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandated conditions tied to appropriations such as acknowledgement of federal funding, prohibitions on dissemination of false information, restrictions on abortion funding, gun control, pornography restrictions, and other appropriation-based constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part 4.2 and subsections 4.2.1–4.2.11 for various mandated conditions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA) Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements and notification procedures for the Notice of Award including associated awards, funding, budget, and additional terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 5.1–5.5 detail what is included in the NoA and recipient responsibilities upon award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and Cash Management
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH payment processes, Smartlink II/ACH procedures, cash requests, interest earned on advances, and improper payment recovery rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 6.1–6.5 outline payment review, cash drawdowns, interest treatment, and compliance with improper payments legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Principles and Allowability of Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental cost principles applicable to NIH awards, including definitions of direct vs indirect costs, allowability of selected items of cost, cost transfers, overruns, allocation of costs, applicable credits, and services provided by affiliated organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 and subparts 7.1–7.9 detail allowability and accounting expectations (see selected items of cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Requirements — Changes in Project and Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and prior approval requirements for changes to project scope, budget rebudgeting, extensions, transfer of performance, charging admin/clerical salaries, supplemental compensation, and other modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes NIH standard terms of award, numerous prior approval categories (8.1.1–8.1.2.17), and requests for prior approval (8.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in Data, Publications, and Sharing Research Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing data rights, NIH Public Access Policy, data management and sharing (DMS), genomic data sharing (GDS), sharing of model organisms, interim research products, and publication/copyright expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8.2 with subparts: Rights in Data; NIH Public Access; DMS Policy; GDS Policy; Sharing Model Organisms; Inventions and Patents; Interim Research Products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Systems and Financial/Property/Procurement Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for institutional financial management systems, program income reporting, property management (real property, equipment/supplies), procurement system standards, approval requirements, and small/minority/veteran-owned business contracting considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 8.3.1–8.3.4 and subparts (financial management, program income, property management, procurement rules including domestic preference and small business contracting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring — Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required reporting during the award: non-competing continuation progress reports, streamlined non-competing award processes, multiyear award progress reports, Final RPPR, financial reports, invention reporting, FCOI reports, research security related disclosures and training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8.4.1 lists report types and 8.4 subsections include record retention, audit, and monitoring expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Award Conditions and Enforcement Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority and procedures to modify award terms, impose specific award conditions, and apply remedies for noncompliance including suspension, termination, withholding of support, other enforcement actions, recovery of funds, and debt collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 8.5.1–8.5.5 describe modification, remedies, enforcement, recovery, and debt collection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout procedures including submission of final Federal Financial Report (FFR), Final Research Performance Progress Report (F-RPPR), Final Invention Statement and Certification, and other closeout documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8.6 and its subparts specify documents and timelines for closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Appeals Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and grounds for administrative appeals related to grant awards and post-award actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8.7 outlines formal appeal channels and required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Program Director/Principal Investigator Applications and Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability, application requirements, review and award considerations, and post-award administration rules when multiple PD/PIs are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9 details requirements for multi-PD/PI leadership structures, eligibility and post-award expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction, Modernization, or Major Alteration & Renovation (A&R) Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, NOFOs, review and award, title to site, matching requirements, procurement and contracting methods for construction, minimum design requirements, labor standards, real property management, allowable/unallowable costs, prior approvals, and closeout for construction awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 10 contains many construction-specific procurement, contracting, and compliance rules (10.1–10.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA — Individual Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, application components, review (overall impact, scored criteria, additional criteria), period of support, stipend levels, allowable/unallowable costs, reporting requirements, changes in project, and other terms (leave, termination, publications, inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11 (11.2.*) outlines detailed NRSA fellowships rules including stipend supplementation, payback, reporting forms, and administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA — Institutional Research Training Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant eligibility, training program director/PI criteria, training program structure, review criteria (overall impact and scored criteria), period of support, allowable/unallowable costs, reporting, and closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11.3 provides institutional training grant-specific policies including trainee appointment forms and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback Requirements for NRSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Service and financial payback obligations, implementation, extensions, waivers, and certification of payback activities for NRSA recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11.4 details payback rules and annual certification forms (PHS 6031-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Career Development (K) Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of K awards, eligibility (institutional and individual), level of effort requirements, application requirements (mentorship, environment, RCR, budget), review (overall impact and scored criteria), allowable costs, reporting, and changes in project including temporary off-site experiences and leave policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 12 outlines mentor requirements, transition awards (e.g., K99/R00), concurrent support rules, and allowable budget categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Applications and Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability and application requirements for modular budget format awards and related review/post-award administration rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 13 covers modular budget thresholds, format, and review implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of Scientific Meetings (Conference Grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, application requirements, public safety & policy requirements (e.g., hotel fire safety), review, funding, acknowledgement of funding source, allowable and unallowable costs, IP/publication rules, and reporting/record retention for conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14 includes safe environment planning and specific allowable/unallowable conference expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for written consortium/subaward agreements, public policy flow-down, allowable/unallowable costs, approval authorities, tangible personal property treatment, and audit expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 15 requires formal written agreements and addresses property and audit provisions for consortium participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to Foreign Organizations and Collaborative International Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility and application review criteria, public policy requirements, funding/payment rules, allowable/unallowable costs, administrative requirements including changes in project/budget, audits, reporting/record retention, and collaborative international award structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 16 addresses foreign applicant expectations and collaborative award structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to Federal Institutions and Payments to Federal Employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, payment processes, VA-university affiliation considerations, public policy requirements, allowable/unallowable costs, and administrative requirements such as equipment accountability and procurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 17 details differences when the recipient is a federal institution and rules for payments to federal employees under grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to For-Profit Organizations (including SBIR/STTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility and special rules for for-profit recipients: cost principles, indirect costs, profit or fee, administrative requirements (equipment, IP, program income, operating authorities, audit), labor distribution requirements, and SBIR/STTR program-specific rules and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 18 and 18.5 include SBIR/STTR fast-track processes, place of performance, minimum effort, required disclosures, and monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Patient Care Costs Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions, policy for charging patient care costs to NIH grants, allowable costs, methods for computing research patient care costs, indirect cost treatment, special procedures for certain hospitals, financial responsibilities, program requirements, and post-award requirements (including rebudgeting change-in-scope considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 19 explains patient care cost categories and notes post-award rebudgeting into/out of patient care costs may be a change in scope requiring prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of Contact — Institutes, Centers, and NIH Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information and responsibilities for NIH ICs, CGMOs, extramural program officials, and other NIH/HHS offices relevant to grants administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part III lists contacts for each institute/center and NIH offices (Closeout Center, OLAW, CSR, OIR, OFM, OIG, etc.) and provides guidance on where to direct specific questions.
